source.author: ov
source.text: Ille caput flavum lauro Parnaside vinctus verrit humum Tyrio saturata murice palla, instrictamque fidem gemmis et dentibus Indis sustinet a laeva; tenuit manus altera plectrum.
source.text_original: Ille caput flavum lauro Parnaside vinctus / verrit humum Tyrio saturata murice palla, / instrictamque fidem gemmis et dentibus Indis / sustinet a laeva; tenuit manus altera plectrum.
source.text_english: That one, his golden head bound with the laurel of Parnassus, swept the ground with a cloak dyed deep in Tyrian purple; and from his left hand he held up a lyre inlaid with gems and Indian ivory, while his other hand held the plectrum.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_original: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis / Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno / palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte / cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_english: Here is that seer, and the trustworthy, no-false son of Phoebus, Mopsus, around whom a scarlet cloak hangs, striking his feet at the bottom; on his brow a helmet bound with ribbons, and on the top of the crest the Peneian laurel.
